How durable systems earn trust

A working excerpt for interface demonstration

A useful research system does not ask you to remember where the evidence lived. It keeps the source close enough to inspect again.

The goal is not a larger reading list. It is a shorter distance between a claim, the passage behind it, and the note you made while thinking.

That distance becomes the difference between collecting material and building understanding from it.

01 / THE READING LOOP

A saved tab is only an intention.

Reader earns its place after “save.” The product carries one source through attentive reading and back into reach when the thought becomes useful.

  1. 01

    Capture the source

    Paste an article URL or upload a PDF. Reader keeps the source and prepares it for focused reading.

  2. 02

    Read without the page

    Web clutter falls away. The text, document structure, reading controls, and your place remain.

  3. 03

    Mark what matters

    Highlight the exact passage, leave a note beside it, or listen when reading is not practical.

  4. 04

    Find the thought again

    Search the library, return through tags and lists, arrange a board, or question the open source with AI.

02 / ONE WORKING LIBRARY

Keep the source, the mark, and the next question together.

01

Sources

Web articles and PDFs live in the same library. PDF text is extracted for search and source-grounded discussion.

02

Reading

A typography-first view keeps highlights, notes, reading progress, and text-to-speech beside the source.

03

Retrieval

Full-text search, tags, lists, and boards give the same source more than one useful way back in.

04

Assistance

Summaries and chat work over material you chose. Reader supports the Fleet gateway or browser-held BYOK keys.

05

Feeds

Authenticated readers can import OPML and refresh RSS or Atom feeds manually, then save an item into the library.

06

Portability

Account data can be exported as JSON. Public sharing is an explicit action, not the default state.

03 / WHY IT EXISTS

“I wanted any article or PDF to become a focused reading and research surface instead of another forgotten browser tab.”
— Product maker note

Capture Mozilla Readability prepares saved web pages; PDF uploads join the same library.

Evidence Highlights remain anchored to the passage that prompted them.

Return Search and organisation operate over the material and notes already saved.

Scope There is no social feed, recommendation engine, or paid team workspace.

04 / CURRENT BOUNDARY

Maintained for real use, not expansion for its own sake.

Reader is a mature personal-use product in maintenance-first support. The owner is not using it enough to justify speculative features, so future work is limited to problems that block the capture-to-reading loop.

Without an account

Start in this browser.

Use the device-local path to capture and read without creating a Reader account.

With Google sign-in

Open the account-backed library.

Saved material is isolated per user; PDFs are stored behind an ownership-enforcing proxy.

Companion tooling

The extension is source-built, not publicly distributed.

The MV3 companion exists for local unpacked installs. A public browser-store release is deferred.

Commercial state

No public plan or checkout.

The repository does not establish a permanent free promise or a paid offer, so this page invents neither.

05 / PRACTICAL QUESTIONS

Before you put a source inside.

Does Reader publish what I save?

No. Libraries are private by default. A shared article or board requires an explicit share action.

What does AI see?

AI features operate on the material you open and ask about. Browser-held BYOK credentials are used per request and are not stored server-side.

Can I install the Chrome extension?

The extension is currently available from source for local unpacked installation. Public browser-store distribution is deferred.

Can I take my data out?

Yes. Reader includes a JSON export for account-scoped articles, boards, and lists.
